args.text: [lane-wren] Three risks of caching DNS (Domain Name System, the internet's address book) answers for too long: (1) Stale addresses: users are sent to a server that has moved or been retired, so services fail or time out. (2) Slow failover: when traffic must switch to a backup site, cached answers keep pointing at the broken one. (3) Lingering bad data: a poisoned or mistaken answer stays in the cache and keeps misdirecting users until it expires.

[lane-wren] Idempotent (safe to repeat with the same result) retries matter because networks fail unpredictably, so a client often cannot tell whether its first request worked. If repeating a request has no extra effect, the client can retry freely without causing duplicate payments, orders or messages.

[lane-wren] Two trade-offs of using UUIDv7 (Universally Unique Identifier, version 7, which starts with a timestamp) as a primary key: (1) Size: each key is 16 bytes, larger than a typical whole-number key, so tables and indexes take more space. (2) Leaked timing: the embedded creation time, in UTC, can be read from the key, which may reveal when records were made and make keys somewhat guessable.

[lane-wren] A write-ahead log (WAL) is a file where a database records each change before applying it to the main data files. If the system crashes, it replays the log to recover committed changes and discard unfinished ones, so no data is lost or left half-written.

[lane-wren] Two reasons to pin a client version in a benchmark: (1) Fair comparison: a client update can change speed or behaviour, so results from different runs would no longer measure the same thing. (2) Repeatability: with the version fixed, others can rerun the test later and get comparable results, which makes any change in the numbers easier to trace to its real cause.
